title: A logger that writes into a list
description:
Write `make_logger(name, lines)`. It returns a `logging.Logger` called `name` that:

- logs every level, from `DEBUG` up;
- appends each message to the list `lines` as text in the form `LEVEL:name:message`;
- does **not** also pass messages to the root logger (`propagate = False`);
- does not add a second handler if `make_logger` is called twice with the same name (it reuses the list from the latest call).

```python
lines = []
log = make_logger("shop", lines)
log.warning("stock low for %s", "tea")
print(lines)        # ['WARNING:shop:stock low for tea']
```
hints: Write a small `logging.Handler` subclass whose `emit(self, record)` appends `self.format(record)` to the list, and give it a `logging.Formatter("%(levelname)s:%(name)s:%(message)s")`.

`logging.getLogger(name)` always returns the same object for a name, so before adding your handler, remove any of your handlers already on it (`log.handlers` is the list of handlers, and `log.removeHandler(h)` takes one off).
unitTests:
@test("formats LEVEL:name:message")
def _():
    lines = []
    log = make_logger("t.one", lines)
    log.warning("stock low for %s", "tea")
    check_eq(lines, ["WARNING:t.one:stock low for tea"])

@test("debug messages are kept too")
def _():
    lines = []
    log = make_logger("t.two", lines)
    log.debug("d")
    log.info("i")
    log.error("e")
    check_eq(lines, ["DEBUG:t.two:d", "INFO:t.two:i", "ERROR:t.two:e"])

@test("does not propagate to the root logger")
def _():
    log = make_logger("t.three", [])
    check_eq(log.propagate, False)

@test("calling it twice does not double the messages")
def _():
    first = []
    make_logger("t.four", first)
    second = []
    log = make_logger("t.four", second)
    log.info("once")
    check_eq(second, ["INFO:t.four:once"])
    check_eq(first, [])
